subject: [RFC PATCH 0/4] mm/zswap: make shrinker writeback work with iocost

reviews.author: Christoph Hellwig
reviews.summary: The reviewer questioned the necessity of REQ_SWAP and expressed concerns about the concept of REQ_SWAP, suggesting that non-swap paging can be just as important for forward progress.
reviews.raw_body:
The issue is that by definition it doesn't need REQ_SWAP then.

Then again the whole concept of REQ_SWAP looks sketchy to me, non-swap
paging can be just as important for forward progress, so if a driver
needs it, it has other issues anyway.

2026-10-05.patch_summary: This patch series aims to improve the performance of zswap shrinker on systems running iocost by addressing two issues: (1) zswap writeback is issued as root and charged to the cgroup afterwards, causing stalls in application allocations; and (2) throttled writes sleep in their submitter, often an application thread. The patches modify zswap to mark writebacks as REQ_BACKGROUND instead of REQ_SWAP, allowing them to be throttled by iocost controllers. Additionally, patch 4 moves reclaim-driven writeback to a per-lruvec kworker, reducing the impact on application threads. The series includes benchmarks showing significant performance improvements for various workloads.
